b: Fault F-01 Power and startup Why will my laptop or computer not turn on? “Will not turn on” covers three different faults: no power at all, power but no picture, and power but no Windows. The lights and sounds tell you which one you have. Get it diagnosed Ask on WhatsApp In short A laptop that will not turn on usually has one of three faults. No power is reaching it (charger, charging port or battery). It powers up but shows nothing (screen, memory or firmware). Or it starts but cannot load Windows (the drive or the startup files). Check the lights first, because each fault has a different fix and a different cost. Fault sheet F-01 Symptom My laptop will not turn on Usual causes Charger, charging port, battery, power cut or surge, memory, drive, motherboard Self-checks 5 checks on this page Diagnostic N$99 , deducted from the repair if you go ahead Handled Workshop in Rundu Get it diagnosed Read the symptom What you see, and what it usually means What you see What it usually means No lights, no fan, no sound at all No power is reaching the laptop: the charger, the charging port, a flat or failed battery, or the power circuit on the motherboard. The charging light is on, but nothing happens when you press the power button The battery, the power button or the motherboard. Lights and fan come on, the screen stays dark The screen, the memory (RAM) or the firmware. See black screen . The maker's logo appears, then it restarts, freezes or says “no bootable device” The drive is failing or the Windows startup files are damaged. It beeps, or a light blinks in a repeating pattern A diagnostic code. HP, Dell, Lenovo and others publish what each pattern means for each model. Self-checks What you can check yourself These are safe to try, cost nothing and do not need tools. Check the charger and the wall socket Try a different wall socket. Look for a light on the charger or beside the charging port, and check the cable for cuts or bent pins. Use the original charger, or one with the same voltage and connector. Do a power reset Unplug the charger and everything connected by USB. If the battery comes out, take it out. Hold the power button down for 30 seconds. Then connect only the charger and try again. Leave it charging for 30 minutes A battery that is completely flat can need time on charge before the laptop will start. Look and listen In a dark room, shine a torch at the screen at an angle. A faint picture means the screen backlight has failed, not the laptop. Listen for the fan, and count any beeps or blinks. Try another screen If lights come on, connect a TV or monitor with an HDMI cable. A picture there means the laptop works and the fault is in its own screen or screen cable. Laptop not turning on when plugged in If the laptop is plugged in and still shows no sign of life, the fault is usually the charger, the charging port or a dead battery. Try another wall socket, look at the charger's own light, and do the power reset in the checks above. If the charger's light is on but the laptop shows nothing, or its charging light flickers, the charging port or the battery is the likely cause. A laptop that is plugged in and charging but still will not start has power and a different fault, such as the screen, the memory or the drive. Laptop not turning on but the power light is on A power light means power is reaching the laptop. If the fan spins and the screen stays black, go to laptop screen black but the power is on . Connect a TV or monitor first: a picture there means the laptop is working and the fault is in its own screen. If the light is on but nothing happens at all, repeat the power reset and disconnect everything plugged into the USB ports. Computer won't start after a power outage A power cut can end with a surge when the power comes back. On a desktop, check the switch on the back of the power supply and the power cable, try another socket, and take the computer off any surge protector that has tripped. On a laptop, test the charger on a different socket. If the charger or the power supply lights up and the computer still does nothing, stop trying: repeated attempts on a damaged power supply can do more harm. A surge can damage the charger, the power supply or the motherboard, and a diagnostic finds which. If the computer starts but complains about the drive or says there is nothing to boot from, the power cut may have interrupted Windows while it was writing, and the files on the drive matter more than the computer. Computer won't start after a Windows update If it was updating when it stopped, leave it alone for an hour before forcing it off: the screen can sit for a long time on "Working on updates" with the drive light busy. If it is stuck for much longer, or restarts in a loop, read Windows Update fails or gets stuck . A computer that goes to a black screen after the update has its own checks on the black screen page. Stop and get it looked at if You smell burning, or the charger or the laptop gets very hot. The battery looks swollen: the case bulges, or the touchpad or keyboard is lifting. Do not charge it. Liquid went into it. Follow the liquid spill steps instead. It stopped during a BIOS or firmware update. Do not keep interrupting it. The drive clicks or grinds and the files matter. b: Fault F-02 Display and startup Why is my laptop screen black when the power is on? If the power light is on, the computer is often running normally and only the picture is missing. Three keyboard shortcuts fix a large share of these. Get it diagnosed Ask on WhatsApp In short A black screen with the power on usually means one of four things: the graphics driver has crashed, Windows is stuck while signing in or updating, the picture is being sent to a different display, or the screen or its cable has failed. Try the keyboard shortcuts below first. If an external screen shows a picture, the laptop itself is fine and the fault is in its screen. Common after an update. The logo shows, then black, every time A graphics driver or a startup fault. You hear Windows sounds, and a torch shows a faint picture The screen backlight has failed. An external monitor or TV shows the picture The laptop's own screen or screen cable. Nothing on either screen, but the fan spins Memory, graphics hardware or firmware. See laptop will not turn on . Self-checks What you can check yourself These are safe to try, cost nothing and do not need tools. Restart the graphics driver Press Windows + Ctrl + Shift + B . The screen blinks and you may hear a beep. This restarts the graphics driver without closing anything. Switch the display output Press Windows + P , then P again, then Enter . Repeat up to four times. This cycles through the display modes, in case Windows is sending the picture to a second screen that is not there. Restart the desktop Press Ctrl + Alt + Delete . If a menu appears, open Task Manager, choose Run new task , type explorer.exe and press Enter. Connect another screen Plug in a TV or monitor with an HDMI cable. If the picture appears there, the laptop is working and the fault is in its screen. Turn it fully off and start clean Hold the power button for 10 seconds until it is off. Unplug every USB device, then start it again. Start in Safe Mode Turn the computer off as Windows begins to load, three times in a row. Windows then opens its recovery screen. Choose Troubleshoot , Advanced options , Startup Settings , Restart , then press 4 . If the screen works in Safe Mode, a driver or a startup program is the cause. You have had to force it off several times. Each forced shutdown risks damaging files. Neither the laptop screen nor an external screen shows anything. b: Fault F-03 Windows Why does my laptop keep showing a blue screen? A blue screen means Windows stopped itself because carrying on could have damaged something. One crash can be ignored. Repeated crashes have a cause, and the stop code points to it. Get it diagnosed Ask on WhatsApp In short Repeated blue screens are most often caused by a faulty driver, failing memory (RAM), a failing drive, overheating or damaged Windows files. Write down the stop code on the screen, because it narrows the cause. Back up your files while the computer still starts, then work through the checks below. Reinstalling Windows only helps when the cause is software. Fault sheet F-03 Symptom It keeps showing a blue screen Usual causes Drivers, memory, drive, heat, damaged Windows files Self-checks 8 checks on this page Diagnostic N$99 , deducted from the repair if you go ahead Handled Remote or workshop Get it diagnosed Read the symptom What you see, and what it usually means These are the usual first suspects for each code, not a diagnosis. The same code can have more than one cause. Stop code on the screen Where to look first MEMORY_MANAGEMENT PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA Memory (RAM), or a driver misusing memory. CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED UNEXPECTED_STORE_EXCEPTION The drive, or damaged Windows system files. DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL SYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLED A driver. If the screen names a file ending in .sys , that file belongs to the driver at fault. INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE The drive, a storage setting in the BIOS, or an update that failed part-way. WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR Hardware: heat, the processor, memory or power. VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE The graphics driver or the graphics hardware. Self-checks What you can check yourself These are safe to try, cost nothing and do not need tools. Record the stop code Photograph the blue screen. Note the stop code and any line that says “What failed”. Think about what changed A new device, driver, program or Windows update just before the crashes started is the first suspect. Unplug new USB devices and uninstall what was added. Back up your files now If Windows still starts, copy your important files to an external drive or cloud storage before doing anything else. Check for heat If the laptop is very hot or the fan is loud before each crash, read laptop overheating . Test the memory Press the Windows key, type Windows Memory Diagnostic and choose Restart now and check for problems . Any error it reports means the memory needs attention. Repair Windows system files Right-click the Start button and open Terminal (Admin) or Command Prompt (Admin) . Run this, and wait for it to finish: sfc /scannow If it reports problems it could not fix, run this and then run the first command again: DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth Look at the crash history Press the Windows key, type reliability and open View reliability history . It shows each crash by date and what failed. Update properly Install pending Windows updates, and get drivers from your laptop maker's support page for your exact model. Avoid “driver updater” programs. Stop and get it looked at if The same stop code keeps coming back after the checks. Windows will not stay running long enough to back up your files. The memory test reports errors. The drive clicks, or files have started to go missing or will not open. On the bench What ADA Tech does We read the crash records Windows keeps, test the memory and the drive, measure temperatures under load and repair Windows if the files are damaged. You are told whether the cause is software or a part, and what each option costs. A standard diagnostic costs N$99. If you go ahead with the repair, that amount comes off the repair cost. Parts are quoted separately, and nothing beyond the diagnostic is done until you have agreed to it. See all prices Questions Common questions Will reinstalling Windows fix a blue screen? Only if the cause is software. If the memory or the drive is failing, the blue screens return on the fresh installation. That is why the hardware is tested first. Can a blue screen damage my files? The crash itself rarely does. But a failing drive is one of the causes of blue screens, and a failing drive does lose files. Back up as soon as the crashes start. Is a blue screen a virus? Rarely. Drivers, memory, the drive and heat are far more common causes. If you also see pop-ups or programs you did not install, read virus and pop-up warnings . b: Fault F-04 Performance Why is my laptop slow? A laptop that is slow, slow to start up or hanging has four common causes. Task Manager shows which one you have in about two minutes, and that decides whether the fix is free, cheap or a part. Get it diagnosed Ask on WhatsApp In short Most slow laptops have one of four causes: a mechanical hard drive instead of an SSD, too little memory (RAM) for what is open, too many programs starting with Windows, or a drive that is nearly full. Open Task Manager with Ctrl + Shift + Esc and look at the Performance tab. A disk at 100% points to the drive, and memory above about 85% points to RAM. Fault sheet F-04 Symptom My laptop is very slow Usual causes Hard drive, memory, startup programs, full drive, heat, malware Self-checks 7 checks on this page Diagnostic N$99 , deducted from the repair if you go ahead Handled Remote or workshop Get it diagnosed Read the symptom What you see, and what it usually means What you see What it usually means Laptop is slow to start up: disk shows 100% in Task Manager, mostly after starting up A mechanical hard drive (HDD), or a drive that is failing. Memory is above about 85% with only a few programs open Not enough RAM for how you use it. Slow for the first few minutes, then fine Too many programs starting with Windows. It slows down when it gets hot and the fan is loud Heat. The processor slows itself to cool down. See overheating . Less than about 15% of drive C: is free The drive is too full for Windows to work properly. It became slow suddenly, with pop-ups or unknown programs Unwanted software. See virus and pop-ups . Self-checks What you can check yourself These are safe to try, cost nothing and do not need tools. Restart, do not just shut down Choose Restart from the power menu. On Windows 10 and 11, Shut down saves part of the system to start faster next time, so only Restart gives a clean start. Read Task Manager Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc and open the Performance tab. Look at Memory and Disk . Under Disk, Windows shows whether the drive is an SSD or an HDD . Turn off startup programs In Task Manager, open Startup apps . Disable anything you do not need the moment the laptop starts. Nothing is uninstalled by doing this. Free up space Open Settings , System , Storage and follow the clean-up recommendations. Aim to keep at least 15% of the drive free. Remove what you do not use Uninstall programs you no longer use, and keep only one antivirus. Windows Security is already built in. Scan for unwanted software Open Windows Security , Virus & threat protection , Scan options and run a Full scan . Install pending updates A laptop that is part-way through updates can be slow until they finish. Laptop is slow to start up If the laptop is slow to start up but fine once it is running, the usual causes are a mechanical hard drive and too many programs starting with Windows. If only one laptop drops while phones stay connected, the fault is in that laptop: its Wi-Fi driver, its power-saving setting or its saved network profile. Compare two devices When the laptop drops, look at a phone on the same Wi-Fi. This one check tells you whether to look at the router or the laptop. Restart the router properly Switch the router off at the wall, wait 30 seconds, switch it on and give it three minutes. Move closer Test beside the router. If it is stable there, the problem is coverage, and the router's position matters more than its settings. Forget the network and rejoin Settings , Network & internet , Wi-Fi , Manage known networks . Choose the network, select Forget , then connect again with the password. Stop Windows switching the adapter off Right-click the Start button and open Device Manager . Under Network adapters , open the Wi-Fi adapter, go to Power Management and untick Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power . Update the Wi-Fi driver Download the wireless driver for your exact model from the laptop maker's support page. Choose the right band If the router offers 2.4GHz and 5GHz, 5GHz is faster over a short distance and 2.4GHz reaches further through walls. Reset the network settings Settings , Network & internet , Advanced network settings , Network reset . You will need to enter your Wi-Fi passwords again afterwards. Switch the router off at the wall, wait 30 seconds and switch it on, then give it three minutes. If you have a separate modem or fibre box, start that first. Look at the lights: if none come on at all, check the power adapter and try another socket, because a surge can kill the adapter or the router. If the lights are normal and every device says no internet, the fault is on the provider's side, and it is worth calling them before changing any settings. Wi-Fi not working on one laptop or on a PC If phones connect and one laptop does not, follow the laptop checks above: forget the network, turn off the power saving on the adapter, update the driver and reset the network settings. b: Guide Reviewed 5 October 2026 Windows 10 support has ended: what to do with your PC Windows 10 still starts and still works, which is why this is easy to ignore. What stopped is the supply of security fixes. Here are the dates and your three options. By ADA Tech Division, Rundu, Namibia. Reviewed 5 October 2026. Short answer Microsoft ended support for Windows 10 on 14 October 2025. A Windows 10 PC still works, but it no longer receives security fixes unless it is enrolled in Extended Security Updates, which for home PCs now runs until 12 October 2027. You have three options: upgrade to Windows 11 if the hardware qualifies, enrol in Extended Security Updates to buy time, or replace the PC. Check which applies before you spend anything. The dates Dates as published by Microsoft, checked 5 October 2026. Date What happens 14 October 2025 Microsoft's support for Windows 10 ended. No more free security fixes, bug fixes or technical support. 12 October 2027 Extended Security Updates for home PCs end. Microsoft first set this for October 2026 and later moved it by a year. What “end of support” means in practice Nothing switches off. The PC starts, your programs run and your files are where you left them. What changes is slower and less visible: Newly discovered security holes in Windows 10 are no longer fixed, unless the PC is enrolled in Extended Security Updates. Over time, new versions of programs and some websites stop supporting it. Microsoft no longer gives technical support for it. The risk matters most on a PC used for banking, business email or client records. Option 1: upgrade to Windows 11 The upgrade is free for an eligible Windows 10 PC. Whether yours is eligible depends on its hardware. These are Microsoft's minimum requirements: Source: Microsoft, Windows 11 specifications and system requirements. Part Minimum for Windows 11 Processor 1GHz or faster, 2 or more cores, on Microsoft's list of compatible 64-bit processors Memory (RAM) 4GB Storage 64GB or larger Firmware UEFI, capable of Secure Boot TPM Trusted Platform Module version 2.0 Graphics Compatible with DirectX 12 or later, with a WDDM 2.0 driver Screen 720p, larger than 9 inches How to check your own PC Open Settings , Update & Security , Windows Update . An eligible PC shows a message that it can run Windows 11. For the detail, install Microsoft's free PC Health Check app and run its Windows 11 check. It names the requirement that fails. To see the TPM, press Windows + R , type tpm.msc and press Enter. Look for Specification Version: 2.0 . A common result is “TPM not found” on a PC that does have one. On many computers, TPM and Secure Boot are present but switched off in the BIOS. Turning them on is a settings change, not a new part. If the check fails on the processor, the PC cannot be made eligible. Option 2: Extended Security Updates Extended Security Updates (ESU) keep security fixes coming to a Windows 10 PC for a limited time. For home PCs, the programme runs until 12 October 2027. According to Microsoft: The PC must run Windows 10 version 22H2 (Home, Pro, Pro Education or Workstations edition) with the latest updates installed. You sign in with a Microsoft account that is an administrator on the PC. You enrol in Settings , Update & Security , Windows Update , where an enrolment link appears on eligible PCs. Microsoft lists three ways to enrol: at no cost if you sync your PC settings, with 1,000 Microsoft Rewards points, or with a one-time purchase of US$30 plus tax. One enrolment covers up to 10 devices. It provides security updates only. No new features and no technical support. Microsoft notes that enrolment options and timing can vary by region. The reliable way to see what is offered in Namibia is to look at the Windows Update page on your own PC. PCs that are joined to a company domain or managed by an organisation are not covered by the home programme. Businesses have a separate, paid programme. ESU is a way to buy time, not a destination. It ends in October 2027. Option 3: replace the PC If the processor is not on Microsoft's compatible list, no upgrade or setting will make the PC eligible for Windows 11. Replacement makes most sense when the PC also has other age problems: a mechanical hard drive, 4GB of memory, a worn battery. Our guide on repairing or replacing a laptop covers how to decide. What not to do Do not ignore it on a PC used for money or client data. Enrol in ESU at least. Do not force Windows 11 onto hardware that fails the check. Microsoft does not promise updates for PCs that do not meet the requirements, which defeats the purpose. Do not install a pirated copy. It adds the risk you are trying to remove. What ADA Tech can do We check whether your PC qualifies and name the requirement that fails if it does not. Where TPM or Secure Boot only needs switching on, that is BIOS work . The upgrade itself, or a clean installation of Windows 11, is part of our Windows packages from N$649 . Your existing Windows 10 licence normally activates Windows 11 of the same edition. Five questions decide both halves of that. By ADA Tech Division, Rundu, Namibia. Reviewed 5 October 2026. Short answer Repair a laptop when the repair costs well under half the price of an equivalent replacement and the laptop can still run a supported version of Windows. Batteries, chargers, memory and a change from a hard drive to an SSD are nearly always worth doing. A failed motherboard on an old laptop, or several parts failing together, usually is not. Get the repair price first: you cannot decide without it. Five questions 1. What has actually failed? You cannot decide until you know. “It will not turn on” could be a charger or it could be a motherboard. A diagnostic costs N$99 with us and comes off the repair if you go ahead. 2. Can it run a supported version of Windows? Windows 10 support ended in October 2025. A laptop that cannot run Windows 11 has a limited future, whatever is repaired. See how to check . 3. What does the repair cost next to a replacement? A common rule of thumb is to stop when the repair passes half the price of an equivalent replacement. Compare with a laptop that would do the same job, not with the cheapest one in the shop. 4. What else is worn? One fault on an otherwise sound laptop is a repair. A dead battery, a cracked hinge, a failing drive and a broken key together are a replacement. 5. Is it fast enough for what you do? b: Guide Reviewed 5 October 2026 How to back up your files, and check the backup works Drives fail without warning, laptops are stolen and drinks are spilled. A backup is the only repair that works for all three, and it takes about twenty minutes to set up. By ADA Tech Division, Rundu, Namibia. Reviewed 5 October 2026. Short answer Keep three copies of anything you cannot replace: the one on your computer, one on an external drive and one somewhere else, such as cloud storage. Set the external drive up with File History so it runs by itself, let OneDrive or Google Drive keep the second copy, and once a month open a file from the backup to prove it works. A backup that has never been tested is a hope, not a backup. The rule: three copies, two kinds of storage, one somewhere else This is usually called the 3-2-1 rule. One copy on the laptop, one on a different device, and one in a different place. Each part covers a different disaster: the second device covers a dead drive, and the copy elsewhere covers theft, fire or a power surge that takes out everything on the desk. What to back up Documents, Desktop and Pictures folders Accounting, invoicing or stock files, wherever that program keeps them Email, if your mail program stores it on the computer Browser bookmarks and saved passwords, by signing in to the browser's sync Photos on the phone, which are a separate backup from the laptop You do not need to back up Windows or your programs. Those can be installed again. Copy 2: an external drive with File History File History is built into Windows 10 and 11. It copies your personal folders to an external drive and keeps older versions of each file. Plug in an external drive that is larger than the files you want to protect. Open Control Panel , System and Security , then Save backup copies of your files with File History . Select the drive and turn File History on. Plug the drive in regularly, for example every Friday. Unplug it and put it away afterwards. Do not leave the drive plugged in all the time. A drive that is always connected is lost to the same theft, power surge or ransomware as the laptop. Copy 3: cloud storage OneDrive is built into Windows and can keep your Desktop, Documents and Pictures folders in the cloud. A free Microsoft account includes 5GB of storage, and paid plans give more. Google Drive is an alternative. The first upload can be large. Do it on Wi-Fi or an uncapped line, not on prepaid mobile data. For an office The same rule applies, with two additions. Decide who is responsible for checking the backup, and make sure the copy kept elsewhere really is elsewhere, not in the same room as the server. See security and backups . Test it Once a month, open the backup and restore one file: a document from the external drive, and a photo from the cloud. If that works, the backup works. If it does not, you have found out on a quiet day and not on the day the laptop died. Mistakes that make a backup useless The only “backup” is a flash drive that also holds the only copy. The external drive lives in the laptop bag, so both are stolen together. The backup was set up once and has not run for a year. Nobody has ever tried to restore a file. The drive is encrypted with BitLocker and nobody saved the recovery key. Check that your key is stored in your Microsoft account. If the drive has already failed Stop using the computer. Every attempt to start it can make recovery harder. Recovery from a failed drive is uncertain and nobody can guarantee it, which is the whole case for backing up first. b: Guide Reviewed 5 October 2026 Genuine Windows and Office: how to check your licence Most laptops that were sold with Windows already carry a licence that survives a reinstall. Two minutes in Settings tells you what you have. By ADA Tech Division, Rundu, Namibia. Reviewed 5 October 2026. Short answer To check Windows, open Settings, then System, then Activation. “Windows is activated with a digital license” means the licence is genuine and tied to the computer, so it activates again by itself after a reinstall of the same edition. To check Office, open any Office program and look under File, then Account. If either one is not properly licensed, there are free legal alternatives, including Office on the web. Check Windows Windows 11: Settings , System , Activation . Windows 10: Settings , Update & Security , Activation . What it says What it means Windows is activated with a digital license Genuine. The licence is stored against this computer's hardware. Windows is activated with a digital license linked to your Microsoft account Genuine, and easier to reactivate after a hardware change. Windows is activated using your organization's activation service A company licence. Normal on a work PC. On a personal PC bought second-hand, ask where it came from. Windows is not activated No valid licence is in use. A watermark appears and some settings are locked. Will I lose the licence if Windows is reinstalled? No, provided the same edition goes back on: Home for Home, Pro for Pro. A digital licence is held by Microsoft against the computer, so Windows activates again when it connects to the internet. Microsoft recommends linking the licence to your Microsoft account, which lets you reactivate after a significant hardware change such as a new motherboard. Check Office Open Word or Excel, then File , Account . It shows the product and whether it is activated. There are two legitimate kinds: Microsoft 365 , a subscription paid monthly or yearly, signed in with your account. A one-time purchase of Office for one computer. Signs that software is not genuine An “Activate Windows” watermark on the desktop. Office repeatedly asks for activation, or shows a red or yellow licence bar. The seller “activated” it with a small program rather than an account or a key. A key was bought for a small fraction of the normal price. Why it matters Security. Activation tools are a common carrier for malware, and they usually have to be run with antivirus protection switched off. Reliability. Keys resold against their terms can be blocked later, without warning. For a business, unlicensed software is a legal exposure. Free and low-cost legal options Office on the web. Word, Excel and PowerPoint run free in a browser with a Microsoft account. LibreOffice. A free office suite that opens and saves Word, Excel and PowerPoint files. Students and teachers. Many schools and universities provide Microsoft 365 through a school email address. Ask your institution. Your existing licence. If the computer came with Windows, you very likely do not need to buy Windows again. b: Guide Reviewed 5 October 2026 Deleted files or a dead hard drive: can the data be recovered? Sometimes. What decides it is what happened to the drive and what has been written to it since. The first hour matters more than the repair. By ADA Tech Division, Rundu, Namibia. Reviewed 5 October 2026. Short answer Stop using the drive now. Files you deleted, or a drive you formatted, can often be recovered if nothing has been written over them. A hard drive that clicks or has failed is uncertain, and a dead SSD is the hardest case. Nobody can promise recovery, and ADA Tech does not. A standard diagnostic costs N$99, and complex data recovery is quoted separately. What to do in the first hour Stop using the drive. Every file saved, program installed or update that runs can overwrite the space where your old files still sit. Do not install recovery software on the same drive. It writes to the drive you are trying to save. Do not keep restarting a drive that clicks or grinds. Each attempt can make damage worse. Do not reinstall Windows or format the drive to see if it helps. That writes over what you want back. Write down what happened. A drop, a power cut, a deleted folder, a Windows update. It tells us where to look. What can usually be recovered, and what cannot General guidance. The real answer depends on the drive in front of us. What happened Usually recoverable? Why Deleted files Often, if you stop at once Deleting removes the entry in the list, not always the data. The data stays until something is written over it. On an SSD it can be cleared sooner. Formatted drive Often, after a quick format A quick format clears the list. A full format, or a Windows reinstall on top, writes over the data. Failing hard disk (clicking, freezing, slow) Uncertain Parts are wearing out. Some files copy, some do not, and every start-up can make it worse. Dead SSD Rarely, and not guaranteed There is no spinning part to repair. When the controller fails, the data can be out of reach. Drive that was in a laptop with liquid or a drop Uncertain Depends on whether the drive itself was damaged. See liquid spills . Phone Not something ADA Tech handles We do not repair or recover phones. Check whether the photos or contacts were synced to your account, and ask the phone maker or a phone repairer. A dead laptop is not always a dead drive When a laptop will not start, the drive that holds your files is often a separate part that is still healthy. It can be taken out and copied to another drive. That is a transfer, not a recovery, and it is much more likely to work. See laptop or computer will not turn on . If the drive is encrypted with BitLocker, you need the recovery key from your Microsoft account before any files can be read. What ADA Tech does We start with a standard diagnostic, N$99, which comes off the repair if you go ahead. It tells us whether the drive is healthy, failing or dead, and whether the laptop is the problem and not the drive. The drive reads normally. We copy your files to another drive. Basic backup or transfer of up to 50GB starts from N$249. The drive is failing or the files were deleted. We tell you what we find and what is realistic. Complex data recovery is quoted separately, and you decide before it starts. The drive has failed physically. We say so, and say whether it is something we can attempt or whether it needs a specialist. We do not promise a result and we do not quote a success rate. Tell us before any work starts which files matter. Message us from anywhere in Namibia for advice, but a drive that has to be examined has to come to the workshop in Rundu. Common questions Can deleted files be recovered? Often, if you stop using the drive straight away. The longer you keep working on it, the more likely the old data is overwritten. Is the Recycle Bin the answer? Check it first. Files deleted normally go there and can be restored in one click. If you emptied it, or held Shift while deleting, they are gone from it and the steps above apply. Can you guarantee my files will come back? No. No technician honestly can, from a drive that is failing or damaged. That is why the backup guide exists: a copy beats any recovery. Once you have the files back Set up a backup so you are never here again. Three copies, one of them somewhere else, and a monthly test. It takes about twenty minutes. See how to back up your files . b: Guide Reviewed 5 October 2026 CCTV installation cost in Namibia: what you are paying for Two quotes for four cameras can differ a great deal and both be honest. The difference is in what each one includes. Here is how to read them. By ADA Tech Division, Rundu, Namibia. Reviewed 5 October 2026. Short answer A CCTV system costs what its parts and its installation cost: cameras, a recorder, a storage drive, cables or power, a router connection for viewing on your phone, and labour. The price moves with the number of cameras, the distance the cable has to run, how many days of recording you want, and whether mains power is available. ADA Tech does not publish a CCTV price. It quotes after a site visit, with every part listed separately, so you can compare like with like. The parts of a CCTV system Cameras. The more of them, and the better their picture and night view, the higher the cost. A recorder (DVR or NVR). It records what the cameras see. The number of camera channels it supports sets how many cameras you can add later. Storage. A hard drive in the recorder holds the footage. A bigger drive keeps more days. Cabling and power. Cable from each camera to the recorder, and power for both. Long runs, roofs and walls add labour and material. Network and remote viewing. Watching from your phone needs the recorder on an internet connection, and mobile data on the phone. Backup power. Without it, a power cut stops the recording. Labour. Mounting, cabling, set-up, and showing you how to use it. What changes the price Number of cameras. Each one adds a camera, a cable run and fitting time. Distance and building. A short run inside one room is cheap. A long run across a yard or between buildings is not. Days of recording. Recording around the clock for thirty days needs far more storage than recording on movement for a week. Picture quality. A camera for reading number plates is a different camera from one that shows a person at a door. Power. Whether there is a plug where each camera sits, and whether a power cut must not stop recording. The same factors apply to the cost of CCTV installation for a home and for a business. A house with a few cameras and short runs is a smaller job. It is not a different kind of job. Wired, wireless or solar with a SIM card Type Suits Watch out for Wired, with a recorder Houses, shops and offices with mains power. The most dependable. The cabling takes the most labour. Plan the cable runs first. Wireless (Wi-Fi) cameras Places where running cable is hard. "Wireless" usually refers to the picture only. Each camera still needs power, and a weak Wi-Fi signal drops the picture. Solar camera with a SIM card Places with no mains power and no cable: a farm gate, a shed, a building site. It needs sun on the panel and mobile signal with data on the SIM card, which you pay for. Shade or no signal and it will not work. Questions to ask any installer How many cameras does this price cover, and what does each camera show? Which recorder is it, and how many more cameras can it take later? How many days of footage will the drive keep, with this many cameras? What is included in the cabling, and what happens if the run is longer than planned? Can I watch on my phone, and what does that need from my internet line? What happens during a power cut? Who is the equipment guaranteed by, and who do I call when a camera stops working? Is the quote written, with every part listed separately? There is no published CCTV price, because it depends on the site. See CCTV installation in Rundu . Point cameras at your own premises.
